DE.AE-02.exposure: Automated activity from outside, including AI-enabled attackers, can arrive at machine speed and look like routine successful requests. Analysis of adverse events should look at how identities are used and at unusual sequences of actions, not only at errors.

use.base_rag: Logs of a model or retrieval setup should show what data was retrieved and sent to the model, so analysis can tell leakage from normal use. See AI RMF: Input and AI RMF: Output.
use.mcp_agentic: Review agent and MCP logs for identity misuse, privilege elevation, tools called in unapproved sequences and actions that succeed but break intent; error-based reviews miss these. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

DE.CM-01.exposure: Automated agents and AI-enabled attackers leave footprints spread across application logs and network traffic. Isolated alerts are often not enough, so network telemetry and audit logs need to be correlated to spot anomalous behavior.

use.base_rag: Send logs from the model or retrieval service into the same central monitoring as network telemetry, so unusual calls to or from it can be correlated. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Centralize MCP events (tool invocations, capability changes, OAuth events, session life cycle) and agent telemetry, and correlate them with network traffic to detect compromised agents. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

DE.CM-03.exposure: Signature-based tools can miss threats from AI agents, which can generate code dynamically or use legitimate system tools. Monitoring user and technology activity needs to include behavior, such as unexpected shell commands, even if the org runs no AI itself.

use.base_rag: Scan code produced by a model for malicious patterns before it is run or merged. See AI RMF: Code generation.
use.mcp_agentic: Apply behavioral monitoring to agent runtimes, flagging unexpected shell commands, lateral movement attempts and obfuscated scripts, and scan generated code before execution. See AI RMF: Agent.

DE.CM-06.exposure: Providers you rely on may start using AI agents, MCP servers or models that touch your data without a change to your contract. Monitor supplier behavior for changes in capabilities or authorization behavior and for relevant advisories.

use.base_rag: Check what data your own systems send to model providers and review those providers' controls and certifications periodically. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Monitor your agents' model calls, tool requests, retrieval pipelines and file handling with providers for unexpected or excessive usage, and track provider release notes for new tools or authorization changes. See AI RMF: Vendor AI and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Scan documents before they enter a retrieval store or model context, since the model will process whatever it is given. See AI RMF: Source data and AI RMF: Input.
use.mcp_agentic: Scan MCP server executables, dependencies and container images before deployment, monitor server processes for unexpected file access or credential reads, and strip active content from files agents retrieve. See AI RMF: MCP / tools and AI RMF: Agent.

use.base_rag: Leadership should set who is accountable for AI use in the org and make sure staff know the rules for what may be shared with AI tools. See AI RMF: Internal process.
use.mcp_agentic: Leadership should fund role-based training for people who approve and run MCP servers and agents, and set when human review or override is required. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.RR-02.exposure: Roles and authorities for handling cybersecurity risk should be clear enough to cover new kinds of outside automated activity, such as agents calling your services. Someone needs the authority to block or disable access quickly when it is abused.

use.base_rag: Assign an owner for each AI use case, including what data it may use and who can switch it off. See AI RMF: Internal process.
use.mcp_agentic: Name who may approve third-party MCP servers, write to the server registry and run emergency disable and rollback; require role-specific training before granting those privileges. See AI RMF: MCP / tools and AI RMF: Agent.

GV.RR-04.exposure: People who join, move or leave may have connected agents or tools to company systems, with delegated access that outlives them. Joiner, mover and leaver steps need to cover agent identities and their credentials, so access is revoked and entitlements removed.

use.base_rag: Staff leaving can leave behind data access granted to AI systems or knowledge sources they set up, so include these in offboarding. See AI RMF: Internal process.
use.mcp_agentic: Give agents and tools their own identities with ephemeral credentials, and revoke them and purge entitlements when an agent is retired or its scope changes. See AI RMF: Agent.

GV.SC-01.exposure: Suppliers can adopt agents and AI services that handle your data, so supply chain policy should set requirements even if you use no AI. These include limiting provider access to the data needed and preventing sensitive data from reaching providers without safeguards.

use.base_rag: Provider policy should limit what data reaches an external model and block sensitive or regulated data from providers lacking safeguards. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Policy should require third-party MCP servers to meet requirements such as code signing, scope minimization and accurate capability declarations. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.SC-02.exposure: Suppliers may use AI models, agents or MCP servers to serve you, and roles and expectations should state who is responsible for what. This includes data isolation, retention limits and how incidents are reported.

GV.SC-04.exposure: Your suppliers may now include model providers, embedding services, tool backends and hosted MCP servers, even when you did not choose them directly. Knowing which suppliers touch your data and how sensitive that access is has become harder.

use.base_rag: Include model and embedding providers in the supplier list, ranked by the sensitivity of data they process. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Include hosted agent offerings, tool backends, memory systems and third-party MCP servers, classified by the data they reach. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.SC-05.exposure: Suppliers may begin using AI agents or tools on your data. Contracts should set data handling and retention terms, breach notification and rapid revocation of access, so a supplier's change in technology does not weaken your protections.

use.base_rag: Contracts with model providers should cover data isolation, retention limits and incident response SLAs for the data sent to them. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Contracts with MCP server providers should require signed code, recorded OAuth scopes and capability declarations, vulnerability disclosure, log access and notification of capability changes. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.SC-06.exposure: Due diligence on a new supplier should ask whether and how they use AI agents or tools on customer data. Standard questionnaires may not cover this.

use.base_rag: Before adopting a model provider, assess where your data goes and how it is isolated and retained. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Assess MCP server providers for accurate capability declarations, OAuth compliance, logging and vulnerability management, and agent service providers for runtime isolation and safety filters applied after audio or image conversion. See AI RMF: MCP / tools and AI RMF: Vendor AI.

GV.SC-07.exposure: A supplier's risk can change quickly when they add AI features, change capabilities or alter authorization behavior, even without a new contract. Ongoing monitoring should look for such changes and for relevant advisories.

use.base_rag: Reassess a model provider's risk when it releases new features or changes how it handles your data. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Monitor your agents' model calls, tool requests and retrieval pipelines with providers for unexpected usage, and review MCP provider release notes for new tools, resources or prompts. See AI RMF: Vendor AI and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.SC-08.exposure: Suppliers that use AI agents or models need to be part of incident planning, because an agent incident at a supplier can move at machine speed. Agree on incident response SLAs and contacts in advance.

GV.SC-09.exposure: Suppliers can add AI features to products you already use. Supply chain monitoring over the life cycle should notice version changes, new capabilities and changed authorization behavior in what they provide.

use.base_rag: Track model and retrieval providers as part of supply chain reviews and reevaluate risk when they change features. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Fold monitoring of agent interactions with third-party services and of MCP provider changes into supply chain risk reporting. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

GV.SC-10.exposure: When a relationship ends, AI-related leftovers can remain: authorizations, tokens, federated identities and data flows. Derived items such as embeddings, tuned model weights and session logs may also persist, so exit steps should cover them.

use.base_rag: At exit, ask for verifiable destruction of embeddings, tuned model weights and logs, not only raw source data. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: At exit, remove allowlist entries, revoke OAuth authorizations and tokens, end data flows and revoke federated identities for the provider's tools. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

ID.AM-01.exposure: Unapproved software that acts on its own can show up on endpoints or in cloud environments without a formal rollout. A hardware and asset inventory that cannot find unmanaged systems will miss assets that bypass normal controls.

use.base_rag: Include hosts and services that run or call models in the asset inventory, with a named owner. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Inventory MCP hosts, clients, servers, gateways and agent platforms with an owner, approved connectivity paths, authorized tools and a risk tier (read-only, write, irreversible). See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

ID.AM-02.exposure: Agent frameworks, MCP clients and servers, and tool libraries can be installed by individuals without any central decision. Software inventory should be able to record such components and their versions, so unknown ones stand out.

use.base_rag: List the models, RAG components and their dependencies that are in use, including those adopted by teams on their own. See AI RMF: Invisible AI usage.
use.mcp_agentic: Include agent stacks, authorized tools, orchestration frameworks and MCP clients and servers in the software inventory. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Map how documents move into a retrieval store and model context, and who may retrieve them. See AI RMF: Source data and AI RMF: Input.
use.mcp_agentic: Map data flows from tool calls and retrievals through back-end systems into model context, note which tools can reach sensitive data, and record transfers outside the org. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

ID.AM-04.exposure: Your services may rely on providers that use AI components, such as model or hosted tool services, behind the scenes. The inventory of supplier services should record what they provide and what capabilities they declare.

use.base_rag: List external model providers and embedding services your org uses, with approval date and owner. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Inventory third-party MCP servers (source, registry status, transport, declared capabilities, assessment results) and the model providers, tool backends, memory systems and hosted agents your agents use. See AI RMF: Vendor AI and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Classify the data that can be placed in a model's context or retrieval store, since it can be returned to users who ask. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Classify tool responses, memory entries and session artifacts, and decide what data may appear in tool parameters and outputs by classification level. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Inventory the knowledge sources and vector stores that feed a model, with their sensitivity and retention. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Inventory agent memory, caches and every data source reachable by tools, including context caches, task state and persisted tool outputs, with the backend system for each. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

ID.AM-08.exposure: Life cycle management should make sure decommissioned systems leave no usable credentials, tokens or data behind, since automated attackers look for leftover access.

use.base_rag: Plan disposal of vector stores and retrieval caches when a use case ends, since residual data can remain. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Record decommission planning for each MCP component and agent, and dispose of agent memory, server caches, stored tokens and session mappings on retirement and on failure paths. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Include model-facing features in vulnerability testing and fix them by the sensitivity of the data they reach. See AI RMF: Output.
use.mcp_agentic: Set remediation times for MCP vulnerabilities such as origin validation bypass or token theft, rank agent vulnerabilities by agent privileges and data sensitivity, and disable vulnerable tools until fixed. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Track advisories for the libraries and services behind your model or retrieval setup. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Track vulnerability sources for agent frameworks, tool adapters, memory systems, MCP servers, OAuth libraries, SDKs and gateway plugins, using vendor advisories, package feeds and CVE databases. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

ID.RA-08.exposure: Disclosures about MCP and agent components can affect you even if you do not run AI yourself, for example via suppliers or software you depend on. Handling should prioritize by exploitability, privileges and exposure, with remediation timelines.

PR.AA-01.exposure: Agents and tools can authenticate with service accounts, API keys or delegated credentials that sit outside normal user lifecycles. The identity inventory and central management need to cover them, preferably through the enterprise identity provider.

use.base_rag: A model or RAG setup that reads company data should use its own service identity, not a person's login. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Manage each agent and tool identity through the central identity provider, with ephemeral or managed credentials and no shared accounts. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.AA-05.exposure: Agents can call APIs or sign in on behalf of users at machine speed, so permissions sized for humans may be too broad. Roles, scopes and actual tool usage need regular review, with unused or excessive permissions revoked.

use.base_rag: Retrieval must respect the asking user's permissions, otherwise the model can return data the user could not open. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Give each AI tool its own scoped credentials, never inherit a user's full rights, and require human approval for write or irreversible actions. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.AT-01.exposure: All staff can be targeted by AI-enabled attackers, for example with convincing, automated messages. General awareness training should reflect that.

use.base_rag: Staff should know what must not be pasted into AI tools and that outputs may be wrong or leak data. See AI RMF: Internal process.
use.mcp_agentic: Staff should know when an agent needs human approval and the risks of autonomous task execution, recursive loops and tool-driven chains of actions. See AI RMF: Agent.

use.base_rag: Train the people who run model features on data safety and on what may be sent to the model. See AI RMF: Internal process.
use.mcp_agentic: Train MCP administrators on registry management, emergency disable, rollback and provenance checks, and administrators and security teams on runtime isolation, credential boundaries and reading agent telemetry. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.DS-01.exposure: Automated attackers and outside agents look for stored data they can reach, including credentials and tokens left in configuration files or logs. Data at rest needs encryption, and secrets belong in a secrets manager.

use.base_rag: Encrypt vector stores, prompt and response logs and caches, which can hold copies of sensitive data. See AI RMF: Source data and AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Encrypt agent memory, server caches and stored OAuth tokens, keep credentials in isolated secret storage injected at runtime, and keep secrets out of prompts, code and logs. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Protect traffic between your systems and an external model or hosted retrieval service, since sensitive data travels in it. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Encrypt tool channels and agent-to-agent messages, require mutual TLS between gateway and server for high-risk deployments, and make server back-end calls use TLS too. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.DS-11.exposure: Backups should include configurations, authorization policies, tool definitions, memory stores and retrieval corpora where these exist. Backups must also be protected so that agents themselves cannot write to or modify them, and restores tested.

use.base_rag: Back up vector stores and retrieval corpora with their indexing metadata, and protect the backups like the source data. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Back up agent memory, tool definitions and authorization policies, and make sure agents cannot write to or alter backups. See AI RMF: Agent.

use.base_rag: Keep retrieval and model services in private, authenticated networks, separated by data sensitivity. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Place agent runtimes, MCP servers and gateways in dedicated segments, isolate third-party servers from your own, and use private authenticated connections to memory and model services. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Version the settings of a model setup, such as prompts and retrieval configuration, so changes can be traced. See AI RMF: Model.
use.mcp_agentic: Version agent prompts, tool lists and parameters, restrict MCP file access to declared roots and process privileges, and harden proxies, load balancers and DNS that carry MCP traffic. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Keep model libraries and serving components on supported versions. See AI RMF: Hosting.
use.mcp_agentic: Set a supported baseline of MCP spec and SDK versions and block production use outside it without a documented exception; remove unsupported agent frameworks and plug-ins and unapproved MCP servers or tool wrappers. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.PS-04.exposure: Logs need to record MCP and agent activity such as tool calls, data accesses, authorization decisions, token events and attempted policy violations. Without them, activity by an external agent acting on a user's behalf cannot be reconstructed.

use.base_rag: Log which sources were retrieved and what was sent to and returned by the model, without storing secrets. See AI RMF: Input and AI RMF: Output.
use.mcp_agentic: Log tool calls, data accesses, authorization decisions and attempted policy violations for each agent. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

PR.PS-05.exposure: Unauthorized MCP servers, tool wrappers and agent components can be installed by individuals and run with their privileges. Use deny-by-default allowlists with integrity checks and install only from approved registries or repositories.

use.base_rag: Control which AI applications and plug-ins staff can install or connect to company data. See AI RMF: Invisible AI usage.
use.mcp_agentic: Allow only approved agent components and tool servers, with versions and integrity checks, from approved registries. See AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Where staff use AI to write code, run it through the same review and testing as any other change. See AI RMF: Code generation.
use.mcp_agentic: Threat-model MCP tools, resources and prompts, secure JSON-RPC handlers and OAuth, and run agent pipelines through dependency scanning, hardening and secret stripping with controlled releases. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Test restoration of retrieval stores and confirm that restoring does not bring back poisoned or incorrect content. See AI RMF: Source data.
use.mcp_agentic: Test that restored agents behave correctly, that restored memory and vector stores do not reintroduce poisoned content, and that restored MCP servers negotiate capabilities matching the approved baseline. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

RS.AN-03.exposure: Root cause analysis for incidents involving agents needs a chain of events that includes tool calls and parameters, resource access, capability changes, authorization decisions and, where available, tool outputs and memory state. Without such records, it is hard to tell what happened.

use.base_rag: Keep prompts, retrieved sources and outputs so you can tell whether data leaked through the model. See AI RMF: Input and AI RMF: Output.
use.mcp_agentic: Reconstruct tool outputs, memory state, retrieval content and policy decisions that led to the incident. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Include model and retrieval providers in your incident notification lists. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Include authorization server operators, gateway operators, MCP library maintainers and model or tool vendors in the incident notification list. See AI RMF: Vendor AI and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Agree with model and retrieval providers how incident information will be shared. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Share agent incident information with internal teams and with model and tool vendors using the contacts kept for agent incidents. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: Vendor AI.

RS.MA-01.exposure: Traditional playbooks may not match the speed of AI-enabled attackers and automated agents. Plans should allow containment steps that can run quickly, such as token revocation and blocking access at the gateway.

use.base_rag: Playbooks should say how to stop a model feature, cut its data feeds and contact the provider when it leaks or misbehaves. See AI RMF: Vendor AI.
use.mcp_agentic: Playbooks should cover prompt injection, tool poisoning, data exfiltration and recursive loops, with token revocation, tool disabling, server isolation and human confirmation, and purging poisoned embeddings. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

use.base_rag: Define thresholds for unusual volume or content in calls to a model service that trigger response. See AI RMF: Output.
use.mcp_agentic: Define escalation thresholds for MCP events (exfiltration through tools, confused-deputy escalation, authorization server compromise, session hijacking) and for agent behavior such as API rate limits and cost spikes. See AI RMF: Agent and AI RMF: MCP / tools.

description: AI-world notes per CSF 2.0 subcategory. `exposure` is shown to every org; `use` only when AI is in use (mcp_agentic when the client's AI areas include MCP / tools or agents, else base_rag). Written by an agent from the CIS MCP and agents companion guides joined to CSF via the official CIS v8.1 -> CSF 2.0 mapping, then reviewed. The Stage 2 XLS writer selects from the intake (AI in use, AI areas).
